body.statement:
For every finite \(X\), fixed \(\ell\), finite \(\mathcal I\ni\varnothing\), and loopless graph pair \(G,H\),
\[
 \mathcal P^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq
 \mathcal P^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{DownCover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H).                         \tag{20}
\]
Consequently, the two zero-allowed joint response-kernel sets are equal if and only if the two directed downward-closed cover conditions hold.  Equivalently, containment holds precisely when, for every exact subgraph \(F\subseteq G\) and every \(C\in\mathcal D_F\), one exact subgraph \(K\subseteq H\) and one tuple \((D,f,a)\) satisfy the source-partition equations and all response equalities simultaneously.  This is a finite-union theorem, not a monotone transfer of exact-support equivalence.
body.proof_tex:
Assume first the law-set containment in (20).  Fix \(F\subseteq G\) and \(C\in\mathcal D_F\).  Exact mixing realization supplies a regime-solvable coefficient matrix with exact support \(F\) and observed mixing \(C\).  Choose the diagnostic source vector \(\xi^C\).  By the stratification lemma its kernel tuple belongs to \(\mathcal P^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(G)\), and hence to \(\mathcal P^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(H)\).  Apply the stratification lemma on \(H\) to the one target mechanism generating this tuple: its actual support is some \(K\subseteq H\), and exact mixing realization puts its observed mixing matrix \(D\) in \(\mathcal D_K\).  Equality of the observational diagnostic law and \(\text{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\) give a surjection and scalars with
\[
 C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}.
\]
For each \(S\), equality of the full kernels, the intervention-pushforward identity, and probability-translation rigidity give \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\).  Thus one \((K,D,f,a)\) satisfies all regimes, proving \(\operatorname{DownCover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\).

Conversely, take any mechanism in \(\mathfrak M^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(G)\).  Its actual support is a unique \(F\subseteq G\), and its observed mixing matrix \(C\) lies in \(\mathcal D_F\) by exact mixing realization.  A downward-cover witness supplies \(K\subseteq H\) and \((D,f,a)\).  Exact mixing realization constructs the target coefficient matrix on \(K\).  Group the original source coordinates over the fibers of \(f\), as in equation (10), and add arbitrary legal sources on zero columns.  The independent-sum and L\'evy--Cram\'er lemmas prove that the resulting common target sources are nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  The proportionality and simultaneous response equations imply the residual proportionalities (11), so intervention pushforward gives equality of every response kernel with the same target mechanism and source tuple.  This target exact-support \(K\)-mechanism belongs to \(\mathfrak M^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(H)\) because \(K\subseteq H\).  Directed containment follows.  Applying it in both directions proves equality.

The proof selected \(K\) only after fixing the exact stratum and \(C\), exactly as the finite condition permits.  It did not infer any inclusion or equality by monotonicity of exact-support law sets; (19) and the diagnostic construction establish the finite downward-closure union explicitly.
body.justification: This theorem explicitly derives the finite downward closure over actual support subgraphs and proves the common-mechanism criterion on the zero-allowed class.
body.gap: Dai et al.'s observational result does not characterize joint intervention kernels or simultaneous response compatibility across regimes.
body.consumer: The same compiler can now compare the zero-allowed convention used in the observational literature without conflating it with exact support.
